messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: increased 5xx rate on serving-runtime (us-west-2) for model:gpt-small -> 14% errors over last 3m. Auto-eviction spike detected on node-17 and node-19. Starting incident thread.
Alex: seeing lots of OOM/container restarts in the logs, plus CUDA illegal memory access thrown by the runtime.
Maria: +1. Dashboard shows CPU spikes then sudden GPU process crash. Stacktrace in logs looks like a deviceaddr fault / misaligned pointer.
Sam: tagging @EngOncall - can you take lead? this looks like live flapping.
EngOncall: taking lead. I'll gather triage steps. first: cordon node-17 and node-19, drain if not critical. Notify customer-facing teams.
Nina: on it - cordoning now: `kubectl cordon node-17` -> CORDONED. Starting drain: `kubectl drain node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (in progress).
deploy-bot: Deploy started: scaled up fallback pool (cpu-inferers) from 4 -> 8 to absorb traffic.
Alex: logs snippet:```
[serving-runtime] ERROR: CUDA illegal memory access at 0x7ffd9a2b0000 (misaligned address)
[serving-runtime] gpu0: kernel panic? signal 11 in kernel module? container killed by OOM-killer
[container] Killed process 4210 (runtime) total-vm:1024000kB, anon-rss:980000kB
```
Maria: here's the model call trace around crash:```
requests: {"seq_len": 4096, "prompt": "..."}
kv_cache_write: pointer offset computed 0x2a but alignment expected 0x10 -> write at unaligned boundary
```
Sam: symptoms match a race in the KV-cache write path after paging/eviction. We recently landed a kernel TLB workaround on the infra nodes last week - might be related.
EngOncall: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon/drain affected nodes (started). 2) route traffic away from nodes with recent kernel patch by updating nodeAffinity for the serving daemonset. 3) enable fallback model-quantized variant on the host-level router to reduce GPU memory pressure. 4) add temporary strict GC on the runtime to avoid overcommit.
Nina: drain completed for node-17. node-19 draining (50% pods moved).
CustomerSuccess: heads-up: we have elevated errors for three customers: acme-inc, beta-shop, analytics-co. CS preparing outreach.
Alex: rolling a config hotpatch to runtime to enable safe-kv-writes (bounds-checked) as a quick mitigation. Rebuild container image and push to canary (canary pool=2 replicas).
deploy-bot: Canary deploy success on canary-pool-3. Healthchecks passing.
Maria: test-run on canary shows no illegal access after safe-kv-writes patch, and CPU fallback handled extra load. Latency up ~60ms but 5xx drops to 0.5%.
Sam: digging into kernel logs on the affected node:```
[kernel] BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000028
[kernel] Code: ... mov    rax,QWORD PTR [rcx+0x28] ...
[kernel] RIP: 0x7f8xxxxx [nvidia_uvm+0x12f4]
[kernel] Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
```
Alex: that RIP points to nvidia_uvm involvement; could be a device driver race when pages are being migrated/evicted. We need SRE infra to confirm driver version mismatch.
Ops: nodes show nvidia-driver 535.54 on node-17, node-19; infra baseline is 535.54 as well but we rolled kernel-5.15.56 -> 5.15.67 last week for security patch.
EngOncall: speculation: kernel change + driver user of pinned buffers is exposing a misaligned address when page migration occurs under heavy eviction. Plan: rollback kernel patch on a single node and test.
Nina: rolled back kernel on node-19 -> rebooting. Monitoring.
CustomerSuccess: acme-inc reports a spike of 502/503s starting 16:12 UTC, lasting ~18 minutes. Escalation open.
Alex: while node-19 reboots, we'll keep canary with hotpatch. If stable for 15m, start rolling restart to apply safe-kv-writes to remaining replicas.
Sam: I ran repro script locally with memory-pressure toggles and got simulated illegal access when eviction timing intersects writes. Patch with alignment checks prevents crash but is higher overhead.
EngOncall: mitigation outcome: canary patch matches and rollback of kernel prevented new OOMs on node-19 post-reboot. We will: 1) schedule controlled rollback of kernel on other nodes in window; 2) plan proper driver upgrade matrix with kernel team; 3) prepare kernel+driver reproducer for nvidia.
deploy-bot: Rolling patch to 80% of serving replicas (safe-kv-writes) started.
Alex: note: temporary cost impact because we scaled up CPU fallback pool and some requests hit quantized variant. Estimated extra cost ~ $1.8k for the incident window.
CustomerSuccess: CS outreach: notified acme-inc and beta-shop; offering log bundles and timeline. Analytics-co had degraded latency but not total failures.
Sam: collecting artifacts: core dumps, dmesg, container logs, perf traces, and repro harness. Uploading to incident bucket: `s3://redwood-incidents/3425012345/`
Maria: added checklist items for postmortem: root cause hypothesis, timeline, mitigation steps, customer impact numbers, rollback procedure, long-term fix (driver/kernel coordination and runtime alignment-safe writes).
EngOncall: handing over to Alex for post-incident actions and postmortem. I'll remain available.
Alex: taking handoff. Next steps: assemble full timeline, confirm driver/kernel matrix with infra, open bug with nvidia (include repro), and plan a non-disruptive runtime redesign for atomic KV updates.
Nina: all modified nodes draining/patching done. Monitoring shows 5xx back to baseline (<0.2%).
CustomerSuccess: CS: acme-inc acknowledged and accepting incident report.
deploy-bot: All patched replicas at 100% by +24m from first alert. No new crashes observed.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error-rate normalized, affected nodes cordoned/unpatched, rollback plan created. Postmortem assigned to Alex, severity: P2, customer-impact: small number of customers with transient failures, duration: ~18 minutes of elevated errors.
Alex: thanks all. Postmortem draft ETA EOD. I'll file follow-ups: BUG-5551 (driver/kernel repro), ENG-OPS-123 (runtime atomic KV rewrite), CS-789 (customer outreach completion). :thumbsup:
EngOncall: handing off final watch to Sam for next 12h.
Sam: acknowledged, will monitor traces and eviction signals.
CustomerSuccess: closing the loop with customers after PM review.
